title.narrative: Middle East Response – Ensuring continuity of treatment and essential services for people affected by HIV, TB and malaria in Yemen, Syria, Iraq, Jordan Lebanon and Palestine. - Western Asia - Multicountry Middle East MER (01-Jan-2025-31-Dec-2027)

description.narrative: Multicountry Middle East MER, Multicomponent, International Organization for Migration (IOM)This program has the following goals: The goal of the 4th phase of the MER is to continue to provide essential HIV, TB, and malaria services to eligible country populations in Syria, Yemen, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon and Palestine, and to migrants and persons in detentions in Libya. To continue essential and successful achievments of MER 3 and pilot and scale-up new interventions for identified priorities (TB, HIV, Malaria) and health sytem strengthening.. To prevent collapse of service delivery for the three diseases in countries affected by conflict and humanitarian crises and continue to strenghten local health systems. The objectives of this program are: TB: To detect and notify cases of new and relapse TB episode during the years 2025 to 2027 as targeted in each of seven countries. TB: To notify and enroll in treatment with 2nd line TB medicines for RR-TB and/or MDR-TB cases in each of seven countries during years 2025 to 2027. TB: To progressively reach an annnual tretament success rate for all forms of TB - bacteriologically confirmed plus clinically diagnosed, new and relapse cases during years of 2025 to 2027. HIV : To promote preventive activities in five target countries.. HIV: To enhance HIV testing coverage among key and vulnerable populations. HIV: To enhance ART coverage for all PLHIV. Malaria: To achieve and maintain universal coverage with LLINs priritizing population at risk of malaria through mass campaigns in the targeted districts in Yemen. Malaria :To strengthen malaria prompt diagnosis and effective treatment at public and community sectors according to the national guidelines at all level in Yemen.. Strengthen and integrate TB,HIV, Malaria surveillance into national health information system using DHIS2
